source.title: A Corrective View of Neural Networks: Representation, Memorization and Learning

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives a theoretical memorization result for arbitrary labels using a random features network and optimization of its output weights; it does not reproduce the original image experiments.
record.gate_note: The introduction cites prior work on random-label memorization, but those cited results are not rows. The paper's own memorization theorem is recorded below. Representation and polynomial-learning results do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Theorem 1 supplies an original theoretical guarantee of arbitrarily small training error for arbitrary labels, including completely random labels, in a two-layer ReLU random features network trained on its output weights.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the memorization conclusion: sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU random features networks can approximate arbitrary labels on bounded, separated points to arbitrarily small training error, with only output weights optimized. The paper also develops representation and polynomial-learning guarantees.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes a two-layer random features network with specially sampled fixed hidden weights and trains only its output weights; it gives a theoretical guarantee rather than the original empirical image-training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee assumes bounded data points with pairwise separation at least θ and uses a width bound depending on n, θ, ε and δ.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference on Computational Learning Theory (COLT), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, vol. 125, 2020
record.problems: The memorization evidence is theoretical and conditional on point separation and a specific random features construction. It reports no image experiment, test error, or direct comparison with fitting true labels.
record.rows_left_out: No other own results in the text measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error; standard deep networks with all layers trained; and an explicit comparison keeping architecture and training hyperparameters unchanged between true and random labels.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs under the same training setup.
Training and test errors across a sweep of label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on memorization and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The theorem's assumptions specify where its support applies; they do not demonstrate failure elsewhere. Unmeasured test error and unchanged training settings do not justify the record's limits_scope label. Arbitrary-input coverage alone supplies no separate result for V3's named input transformations.

versions.untested_parts: The theorem does not test image datasets, test error at chance, or whether the architecture and training hyperparameters remain unchanged from true-label training.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network
rows.size_stated: N meets the lower bound in Theorem 1; the bound is stated in terms of n, θ, ε, δ
rows.stage_stated: random features; only output weights are free parameters
rows.operation_detail: Draw random features (ωj,Tj) and optimize coefficients aj with SGD/GD; the objective is convex and SGD/GD obtains the optimum.

conditions.value: arbitrary x1,…,xn ∈ Rd with ||xk|| ≤ 1 and pairwise distance at least θ

rows.measure: Sum of squared errors on the n training points
rows.value: At most ε, with probability at least 1−δ, when N satisfies the Theorem 1 lower bound
rows.note: This is a theorem for a specially sampled random features model, with only output coefficients optimized. It establishes approximate training interpolation for arbitrary labels, but gives no test-error result or comparison with training on true labels.
rows.check: Change partial to observed: the guaranteed training squared error is at most any prescribed ε, rather than a weak or incomplete fitting effect. The restricted model and unmeasured test error belong in the condition and untested parts. Distinguish existence of coefficients achieving ε from optimization to finite accuracy; Section 1.4 describes GD approaching the optimum.

relationships.condition: Bounded, pairwise-separated inputs; sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU network with sampled, fixed hidden features and optimized output weights.
relationships.reason: R1 guarantees training squared error at most ε with probability at least 1−δ for arbitrary labels; Theorem 1 also states that output-weight SGD/GD reaches the convex optimum.
relationships.display_finding: Training squared error is at most ε with probability at least 1−δ for arbitrary labels, and output-weight SGD or GD reaches the convex optimum.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Theorem 1 setting: separated arbitrary points and a two-layer random features ReLU network
reader_labels.reason: The theorem guarantees training squared error at most ε for arbitrary labels under its stated width and sampling conditions (R1), but does not test chance-level test error or unchanged settings relative to true-label training.
